notes: Addresses independently reproduced bridge lifecycle defects behind repeated Control PIN prompts. Each WebView page now has unique request ownership; old-page replies cannot resolve new-page requests. Requests capture page/session/grant generations when submitted, preventing queued old Lock commands from revoking a newly promoted grant, including the interval before the UI reload runs. Existing authorization, real grant expiry, explicit Lock, Control eligibility and App revocation remain enforced. No re-enrollment or credential reset is needed; compatible with the current scoped-device Backend protocol (test.38 and later), no new Backend required for this Android fix. Connection diagnostics are available through Android Back > Connection diagnostics: local RAM-only version/role/grant timing and bounded event labels, no PINs, keys or addresses. All42 non-browser regression scripts passed, including actual full bundled UI reproduction of the1.0.13 stale-response-to-Lock sequence, fixed1.0.14 comparison, JVM native-guard harness and actual Backend HTTP integration. Independent native and UI review passed. These tests reproduce concrete defects, but physical Android/Fire Tablet resolution still requires device acceptance testing. Original signing identity retained; iPad unchanged and no iOS update included.
